spec.purpose: New whole-provider DLL with unchanged packaged CLI, CK, FLA and MoE: one original q8192/out512 read-only input-row reuse audit. Hashes propose row representatives; all original BF16 words of each proposed match are compared on the GPU before counting any reusable row. All original producers, candidates and K16 replays still execute. There is no implemented reuse cache or candidate speed measurement. Every raw GB10 token, first-logit tolerance0.125 and actual callback must pass. No long-context, package soak or performance qualification transfers.

decision: Do not implement whole-input-row replay caching for the current product route. The real q8192 run finds7935 duplicate inputs only in each of the first four layer0 projections; the other166 calls have no bit-identical rows and there are no hash collisions. Even the loose bound is6366393 of432889515 original candidates (about1.47068%), before lookup, cache and scatter overhead. Keep the read-only audit default off. It preserves all512 GB10 outputs and callbacks, but executes no actual reuse and qualifies no candidate performance or release.
scope: One new process loads the real model and performs the original q8192/out512 request with the read-only row audit enabled. All268 archived runtime assets are verified; only the compiled whole-provider is overridden. Its source differs from the prior original-control whole provider only by the audit include and call. Every original producer, selector and exact K16 replay still executes. Position-sensitive hashes propose representatives, and the GPU compares every BF16 word before counting duplicate inputs. Hash collisions are unproven rows and cannot establish reuse. The potential saved-candidate count is capped by both original candidates and verified duplicate-output cells plus all unproven collision-row cells for each projection; this is a loose upper bound, not implemented reuse or measured savings. Each original GB10 output ID, actual callback and prompt-bound first logit is attached. Earlier control counts are explicitly comparable diagnostics, not a same-DLL timing pair. No prefix, long-context, package-soak, retained-performance or release qualification follows.
